fr: Je prends un café noir.
en: I'm having a black coffee.
notes: The final ds in prends is silent, so prends and prend sound identical.

fr: Elle boit un chocolat chaud.
en: She is drinking a hot chocolate.
notes: The final t of chocolat and the final d of chaud are both silent.

fr: Nous allons au café ce matin.
en: We are going to the café this morning.
notes: Nous allons requires a liaison, so the silent s links to the next vowel as a z sound.

fr: Ils arrivent à la terrasse.
en: They are arriving at the terrace.
notes: The liaison between ils and arrivent turns the silent s into a z sound.

fr: Le café est très chaud.
en: The coffee is very hot.
notes: The final d in chaud is never pronounced.

fr: Les clients attendent leur commande.
en: The customers are waiting for their order.
notes: The verb ending ent in attendent is completely silent.

fr: Elle prend un thé avec du citron.
en: She is having a tea with lemon.
ipa: /ɛl pʁɑ̃ œ̃ te a.vɛk dy si.tʁɔ̃/
notes: The final d of prend is silent, just like in the form prends.

fr: Il commande deux croissants.
en: He is ordering two croissants.
notes: The final s of croissants is silent even though the word is plural.

fr: Nous partageons une tarte aux pommes.
en: We are sharing an apple tart.
notes: The ending ons in partageons keeps a nasal sound, not two separate letters.

fr: Les serveurs sont très gentils.
en: The waiters are very kind.
notes: The final s of serveurs and of gentils both stay silent.

fr: Elle demande l'addition au serveur.
en: She is asking the waiter for the bill.
notes: La becomes l' before addition since the word starts with a vowel sound.

fr: Il boit son café sans sucre.
en: He drinks his coffee without sugar.
notes: Son and sans share a similar nasal sound but are spelled very differently.

fr: Elles commandent une salade.
en: They are ordering a salad.
notes: Elles commandent sounds identical to elle commande despite the plural subject.

fr: Le garçon apporte les verres.
en: The waiter brings the glasses.
notes: The final s of verres is silent even though it marks the plural.

fr: Nous choisissons une table en terrasse.
en: We are choosing a table on the terrace.
notes: The ending ons in choisissons keeps one nasal sound, not two separate letters.

fr: Il paie l'addition tout de suite.
en: He pays the bill right away.
notes: Paie is pronounced like pè, the final e stays silent.

fr: Elle aime le café au lait.
en: She likes coffee with milk.
notes: Aime ends in a silent e that is never pronounced.

fr: Les tasses sont sur la table.
en: The cups are on the table.
notes: The final s of tasses stays silent even though it shows the plural.

fr: Il retrouve ses amis au café.
en: He is meeting his friends at the café.
notes: Ses amis needs a liaison, so the silent s becomes a z sound.

fr: Elle prend deux sucres dans son café.
en: She takes two sugars in her coffee.
ipa: /ɛl pʁɑ̃ dø sykʁ dɑ̃ sɔ̃ ka.fe/
notes: Deux ends with a silent x that is never heard.

fr: Nous payons chacun notre part.
en: We each pay our own share.
notes: Payons keeps the nasal on sound spelled with the letters ons.

fr: Ils préfèrent la salle plutôt que la terrasse.
en: They prefer the indoor room rather than the terrace.
ipa: /il pʁe.fɛʁ la sal ply.to kə la tɛ.ʁas/
notes: Préfèrent ends in a silent ent, sounding just like the singular préfère.

fr: Le serveur apporte l'addition.
en: The waiter brings the bill.
notes: Le becomes l' before addition since the word starts with a vowel sound.

fr: Elle laisse un petit pourboire.
en: She leaves a small tip.
notes: The final t of petit is silent before a consonant sound.

fr: Nous restons assis à l'intérieur.
en: We stay seated inside.
notes: Restons assis needs a liaison, so the silent s links as a z sound.

fr: Il boit son café d'un trait.
en: He drinks his coffee in one gulp.
notes: D'un links de and un together, dropping the vowel of de.

fr: Les croissants sont encore chauds.
en: The croissants are still warm.
notes: Sont encore takes a liaison, so the normally silent t is pronounced.

fr: Elle commande la même chose que lui.
en: She orders the same thing as him.
ipa: /ɛl kɔ.mɑ̃d la mɛm ʃoz kə lɥi/
notes: Même ends in a silent e that simply softens the m sound.

fr: Ils partagent l'addition à la fin.
en: They split the bill at the end.
notes: L' replaces la before addition because the word begins with a vowel sound.

fr: Elle a commandé un café crème.
en: She ordered a coffee with milk.
notes: Commandé, commander and commandez all sound the same; only spelling shows the tense.

fr: Nous allons prendre un dessert.
en: We are going to have a dessert.
notes: Allons needs a liaison, so the silent s links to the next vowel.

fr: Il a payé l'addition avant de partir.
en: He paid the bill before leaving.
ipa: /il a pɛ.je la.di.sjɔ̃ a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ/
notes: Payé sounds exactly like payer and payez, even though the tense differs.

fr: Nous avons laissé un bon pourboire.
en: We left a good tip.
notes: Laissé sounds identical to laisser, even though the tense is different.

fr: Elle va commander une salade.
en: She is going to order a salad.
notes: Commander ends in a silent r, so it sounds just like commandé.

fr: Ils ont pris leurs cafés à emporter.
en: They took their coffees to go.
notes: Ont and on sound identical, but only ont means they have.

fr: On a réservé une table en terrasse.
en: We reserved a table on the terrace.
ipa: /ɔ̃ a ʁe.zɛʁ.ve yn tabl ɑ̃ tɛ.ʁas/
notes: On is pronounced exactly like ont, so context decides the spelling.

fr: Elle est allée au café avec sa sœur.
en: She went to the café with her sister.
ipa: /ɛl ɛ.t‿a.le o ka.fe a.vɛk sa sœʁ/
notes: Allée takes an extra silent e to agree with the feminine subject elle.

fr: Nous avons trouvé la tarte délicieuse.
en: We found the tart delicious.
notes: Trouvé stays masculine here because the direct object comes after the verb.

fr: Les cafés qu'elle a commandés étaient froids.
en: The coffees she ordered were cold.
ipa: /le ka.fe kɛl a kɔ.mɑ̃.de e.tɛ fʁwa/
notes: Commandés adds a silent s to agree with cafés, placed before the verb.

fr: Il va payer l'addition tout à l'heure.
en: He is going to pay the bill in a moment.
notes: À in tout à l'heure needs its accent, unlike the verb form a.

fr: Nous avons discuté ou nous avons juste bu un café.
en: We chatted, or we just had a coffee.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ dis.ky.te u nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʒyst by œ̃ ka.fe/
notes: Ou without an accent means or, while où with an accent means where.

fr: Elle a demandé où se trouvaient les toilettes.
en: She asked where the restrooms were.
ipa: /ɛl a də.mɑ̃.de u sə tʁu.vɛ le twa.lɛt/
notes: Où keeps its accent because it means where, unlike the conjunction ou.

fr: Ils vont bientôt fermer le café.
en: They are going to close the café soon.
notes: Fermer ends in a silent r, so it sounds the same as fermé.

fr: Nous avons partagé l'addition à la fin du repas.
en: We split the bill at the end of the meal.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ paʁ.ta.ʒe la.di.sjɔ̃ a la fɛ̃ dy ʁə.pa/
notes: Partagé is distinguished from partager only by spelling, not by sound.

fr: Elle a acheté deux croissants qu'elle a partagés avec moi.
en: She bought two croissants that she shared with me.
ipa: /ɛl a aʃ.te dø kʁwa.sɑ̃ kɛl a paʁ.ta.ʒe a.vɛk mwa/
notes: Partagés takes a silent s to agree with the plural croissants placed earlier in the sentence.

fr: Il faut que tu viennes au café avec nous.
en: You need to come to the café with us.
ipa: /il fo kə ty vjɛn o ka.fe a.vɛk nu/
notes: Viennes in the subjunctive is pronounced with an audible n, unlike the indicative vient.

fr: Je ne pense pas qu'il finisse son café à temps.
en: I don't think he will finish his coffee in time.
ipa: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kil fi.nis sɔ̃ ka.fe a tɑ̃/
notes: Finisse in the subjunctive is spelled with a double s, unlike the indicative finit.

fr: C'est le café où nous nous sommes rencontrés.
en: This is the café where we met.
ipa: /sɛ lə ka.fe u nu nu sɔm ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe/
notes: Rencontrés agrees with the plural subject nous, adding a silent s.

fr: Ce serveur est plus rapide que celui d'hier.
en: This waiter is faster than yesterday's.
ipa: /sə sɛʁ.vœʁ ɛ ply ʁa.pid kə sə.lɥi djɛʁ/
notes: Ce before a noun is a demonstrative, not to be confused with the pronoun se.

fr: Elle se demande si le café est encore ouvert.
en: She wonders if the café is still open.
ipa: /ɛl sə də.mɑ̃d si lə ka.fe ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ u.vɛʁ/
notes: Se before the verb is a reflexive pronoun, unlike the demonstrative ce.

fr: Ces cafés coûtent plus cher que ses habitudes ne le permettent.
en: These coffees cost more than his habits allow.
ipa: /se ka.fe kut ply ʃɛʁ kə se a.bi.tyd nə lə pɛʁ.mɛt/
notes: Ces, ses and c'est are all pronounced the same but never interchangeable in writing.

fr: C'est le meilleur café du quartier.
en: It's the best café in the neighborhood.
notes: C'est contracts cela est and sounds exactly like ces and ses.

fr: Quel café préfères-tu, celui-ci ou celui-là.
en: Which coffee do you prefer, this one or that one.
ipa: /kɛl ka.fe pʁe.fɛʁ ty sə.lɥi.si u sə.lɥi.la/
notes: Quel agrees with the masculine noun café, unlike the feminine form quelle.

fr: Quelle terrasse préférez-vous en été.
en: Which terrace do you prefer in summer.
notes: Quelle takes the extra silent e to agree with the feminine noun terrasse.

fr: Bien qu'il soit tard, le café reste ouvert.
en: Although it is late, the café stays open.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil swa taʁ lə ka.fe ʁɛst u.vɛʁ/
notes: Soit is the subjunctive of être and must not be confused with the word soi.

fr: Je doute que ce serveur se souvienne de notre commande.
en: I doubt this waiter remembers our order.
ipa: /ʒə dut kə sə sɛʁ.vœʁ sə su.vjɛn də nɔtʁ kɔ.mɑ̃d/
notes: Se souvienne uses the subjunctive with an audible final n, unlike se souvient.

fr: Les clients ont attendu longtemps avant qu'on les serve.
en: The customers waited a long time before they were served.
ipa: /le kli.jɑ̃ ɔ̃.t‿a.tɑ̃.dy lɔ̃.tɑ̃ a.vɑ̃ kɔ̃ le sɛʁv/
notes: Serve in the subjunctive drops the final t found in the indicative form sert.

fr: C'est la première fois qu'elle vient dans ce café.
en: It's the first time she has come to this café.
ipa: /sɛ la pʁə.mjɛʁ fwa kɛl vjɛ̃ dɑ̃ sə ka.fe/
notes: C'est here cannot be replaced by ses or ces, even though all three sound alike.

fr: Il semble que les prix aient encore augmenté.
en: It seems that prices have gone up again.
ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə le pʁi ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ o.gmɑ̃.te/
notes: Aient, the plural subjunctive of avoir, is pronounced just like the singular ait.

fr: Nous aimerions nous asseoir en terrasse, si cela ne vous dérange pas.
en: We would like to sit on the terrace, if that doesn't bother you.
ipa: /nu.z‿ɛ.mə.ʁjɔ̃ nu.z‿a.swaʁ ɑ̃ tɛ.ʁas si sə.la nə vu de.ʁɑ̃ʒ pa/
notes: Aimerions in the conditional needs a liaison right after nous.

fr: Quelles que soient ses habitudes, il commande toujours la même chose.
en: Whatever his habits are, he always orders the same thing.
ipa: /kɛl kə swa.t se a.bi.tyd il kɔ.mɑ̃d tu.ʒuʁ la mɛm ʃoz/
notes: Ses here is a possessive pronoun, not to be confused with c'est or ces.

fr: Il est possible que le serveur ait oublié notre commande.
en: It is possible that the waiter forgot our order.
ipa: /il ɛ pɔ.sibl kə lə sɛʁ.vœʁ ɛ.t‿u.bli.je nɔtʁ kɔ.mɑ̃d/
notes: Ait, the subjunctive of avoir, sounds exactly like the noun est or the verb es.

fr: Bien que ce café soit cher, il reste toujours plein.
en: Although this café is expensive, it is always full.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə sə ka.fe swa ʃɛʁ il ʁɛst tu.ʒuʁ plɛ̃/
notes: Ce before café is the demonstrative adjective, unlike the pronoun se in reflexive verbs.

fr: Les touristes ne savent pas quels cafés sont les plus authentiques.
en: The tourists don't know which cafés are the most authentic.
ipa: /le tu.ʁist nə sav pa kɛl ka.fe sɔ̃ le plyz‿o.tɑ̃.tik/
notes: Quels agrees with the plural masculine cafés, adding a silent s.

fr: Il faut absolument que nous choisissions une table à l'ombre.
en: We absolutely need to choose a table in the shade.
ipa: /il fo.t‿ab.sɔ.ly.mɑ̃ kə nu ʃwa.zi.sjɔ̃ yn tabl a lɔ̃bʁ/
notes: Choisissions in the subjunctive adds an extra syllable not heard in the indicative form.
